title: Bodhicitta
hook: the mind that wants to wake up for the sake of all beings

segments.voice: Yesterday: lojong, mind training in short slogans, like drive all blames into one. Your line: one slogan.

Every flight, the same speech. If the cabin loses pressure, put on your own mask first, then help the person next to you. Nobody can help anyone after passing out. Now take it one step further. Someone puts on their own mask only so they can help the person beside them. And the row behind. And every passenger on every plane. In Mahayana and Tibetan Buddhism, that is the reason given for walking the path at all.
screen: `PUT ON YOUR OWN MASK FIRST.` → `ONLY TO HELP THE NEXT PERSON.` → `AND EVERY PASSENGER, EVERYWHERE.`

segments.voice: Bodhicitta. Bodhi, awakening, the word you met under the tree. Citta, mind or heart. The awakening mind: the wish to wake up not just for yourself, but so you can help every being do the same. In Tibetan practice it's the engine of everything. The four thoughts turn the mind; bodhicitta tells it where to go. One teacher Tibetans study closely on bodhicitta is Shantideva, an Indian monk. A story people tell: at the monastery of Nalanda, the other monks thought he was lazy, good only for eating, sleeping and strolling around. To embarrass him, they asked him to teach in public. He sat down and recited a whole long poem, The Way of the Bodhisattva, and the monks were stunned. In it he draws a simple line: there's wanting to go on a journey, and there's actually setting out. Bodhicitta has both: the wish, then the steps, in giving, patience, effort and the rest. Near its close comes a vow people still say today, in paraphrase: for as long as space remains and beings remain, may I remain too, to ease the world's suffering. Here the traditions differ, so it's worth saying who says what. In the Theravada, the elders honor the bodhisattva's road as the Buddha's own long path through the Jataka lives, and the usual aim is awakening as an arahant, though some Theravada Buddhists take up the bodhisattva path too. In the Mahayana and the Vajrayana, bodhicitta is placed at the start of the path for everyone. That's why Tibetan practices end by dedicating whatever good was done to all beings. Not for me. For all of us.
screen: `BODHI, AWAKENING. CITTA, MIND.` · `SHANTIDEVA AT NALANDA.` · `WANTING TO GO, THEN SETTING OUT.` · `AS LONG AS SPACE REMAINS.` · then, large: `FOR ALL OF US.`

segments.voice: Before you sit, silently set the intention: whatever good comes from this, may it help someone, and then widen it: may it help everyone. Sit with the breath as usual; you don't need to feel anything special. At the end, if you'd like, give it away once more: whatever good came from this, for all of us.
Bodhicitta. The awakening mind: the wish to wake up for the sake of all beings, and the steps that follow the wish.
Your line: for all of us. The wish, and then the steps. Day three hundred twelve is in the books.

howItsDone: Mahayana and Tibetan Buddhists generate bodhicitta at the start of practice, often reciting a short refuge and bodhicitta verse, and end by dedicating the merit to all beings; many also take formal bodhisattva vows.

original.note: Sanskrit bodhicitta: bodhi (awakening) + citta (mind, heart). Tibetan: jangchub sem.

trapdoor: what you thought: being a nice person.
what it means: the wish to wake up fully for the sake of all beings, and the practice that follows.
what a scholar hears: Shantideva's Bodhicaryavatara (1.15–16) distinguishes aspiring bodhicitta from engaged bodhicitta with the image of wishing to go and actually going.
